subject: Atlas Health — dedicated cluster saturation and remediation plan
messages:

To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@atlashealth.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe latency / timeouts on dedicated cluster this morning

Hi Sean / Monica,

We started seeing large queue times and token generation timeouts against our dedicated pool this morning (~07:40 PDT). Multiple customer-facing endpoints returned 503/504 and our observability shows GPU utilization pegged at 99% with long scheduling delays. This impacted our ML-driven triage flows for about 20 minutes but created a significant user-facing incident for a handful of enterprise customers.

Can you confirm whether this was a Redwood side saturation / autoscale lapse, or something on our config? We need a short timeline + immediate mitigation we can share with our stakeholders.

Attaching our ops snippet (small).

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Nguyen
Head of Platform Engineering
Atlas Health

Laura — thanks for the report and the snippet. Apologies for the disruption.

Quick update: we are investigating a saturation event in your dedicated GPU pool that aligns with the timestamps you provided. Monica and our infra team (cc: Dev) are taking lead. Initial ask: can you confirm whether there were any sudden traffic pattern changes (batch jobs, overnight replays) around 07:30–07:50 PDT? That will help rule out client-side load spikes.

I'll keep this thread for customer-facing updates; internal triage notes will be on the INC ticket I just created (link below).

Immediate next steps we are executing:
- Enabling short burst capacity on the pool to relieve queued requests
- Tracing scheduling latencies to identify any degraded hosts
- Looking for autoscale controller errors and any failed instance launches

We aim to have an initial findings note within 90 minutes.

—Sean

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 08:48:00 -0700
Subject: [internal] Triage: Atlas Health dedicated GPU pool saturation

Internal notes (copying timeline as we go):

Observed:
- 07:38 PDT: Scheduler latency jumps; queue depth increases
- 07:39 PDT: Three instances failed health checks and were marked degraded
- 07:40–07:55 PDT: Autoscaler attempted to launch replacements; two launch attempts timed out due to NVLink driver init error (root cause candidate)

Mitigation applied:
- Forced short burst (cold-start warm pool) to serve pending requests — reduced queue within ~4m
- Manually removed two failing hosts from rotation to prevent noisy neighbor impact

Action items:
- Dev to collect instance-level logs and driver traces (assigned)
- Engineering to validate autoscaler backoff policy and CVE/regression from recent infra stack changes
- Prepare customer-facing summary and ETA for full RCA

Dev — pls attach logs to the INC ticket and flag if you see a driver regression.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Sr. Product Manager, Dedicated Capacity

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Laura Nguyen <laura@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Atlas Health — post-incident summary and next steps (RCA attached)

Laura — thanks again for patience. Attached is our customer-facing RCA and the instance trace logs you requested. Summary below you can share with your CISO: 

One-paragraph summary (shareable):
On 2026-03-20 at ~07:38 PDT, Atlas Health's dedicated GPU pool experienced a scheduler saturation event caused by two concurrent driver initialization failures on replacement instances, which delayed autoscaler recovery. While no customer data was exposed, queued requests experienced increased latency and some token-generation requests failed (503/504) for approximately 12–18 minutes. Service recovery was reached by 07:55 PDT after manual removal of degraded hosts and enabling short-burst capacity.

Key details (short):
- RCA: Two replacement instances failed NVLink driver init during autoscaler launches due to a packaging regression in the GPU driver bundle. The autoscaler retried with exponential backoff which extended the recovery window.
- Impact: Elevated queue depth and 503/504 responses for ~12–18 minutes across your dedicated pool; no cross-tenant data leakage detected.
- Fixes applied: Manual host removal, temporary burst capacity, hotfix to driver packaging pushed to stable pool images, autoscaler backoff policy adjusted to reduce overall retry window during driver-init failures.
- Deliverables: Attached PDF RCA (rca_gpu_pool_20260321.pdf) and raw trace logs (instance-logs-trace-03-20.txt). We will also provide a sandboxed reproduction plan and unit-tests for the driver packaging step.

Recommended client-side guardrails (short):
- Implement short client-side retry jitter and exponential backoff for idempotent token generation requests
- Monitor queue depth and set alerting thresholds at 60% of your SLA target to catch early buildup

Next steps:
- We will schedule a 30-minute review call to walk the RCA and your questions. Proposed windows: Mon 03/22 09:00–10:00 PDT or 14:00–14:30 PDT. Please confirm.
- We will follow up with a post-release verification run and provide logs verifying the hotfix rollout.

Attachments: rca_gpu_pool_20260321.pdf, instance-logs-trace-03-20.txt

If you'd like a redactable one-paragraph statement for external communications, we can provide that as well.

—Sean
